newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sell-offs unaffected by annulment - minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sell-offs unaffected by annulment - minister.

text.p: Turkish state minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Friday the country's privatisation plans would not be affected by a constitutional court annulment of an article banning the sequestration of state-owned assets. "This decision will in no way affect privatisation procedures and auctions. The issue purely concerns the payments interest and debt owed by state enterprises to banks," Soylemez, the minister responsible for the treasury and privatisation, told Reuters.
The constitutional court earlier on Friday cancelled an article prohibiting the sequestration of all assets owned by state enterprises slated for privatisation.
The law had taken effect in November 1994 to enable the sell-off of state enterprises or their assets and properties as part of Turkey's privatisation drive.

The article cancelled by the court had prohibited all proceedings to sequestrate assets of such state institutions. Separate courts in Turkey had applied to the constitutional court to have the article cancelled.
Soylemez said the cancellation would lead to an increase in outstanding interest payments and losses of state enterprises.
"This article was helpful to the privatisation board in restructuring the state enterprises, preparing them for privatisation and reducing their losses," Soylemez said.
"But privatisation will continue, with its new impetus and high performance, in accordance with the law," he added.

Turkey's stumbling efforts to privatise state firms -- in line with a plan launched more than 10 years ago -- were given a boost last week when the constitutional court gave the go-ahead for the privatisation of the state telecommunications company.
The court had annulled the sell-off several times before.
